records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — Evaluating timezone.now() as a dataclass default gives every source created by a process the same stale queued timestamp, making queued-time metadata incorrect.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a Python gotcha. In the diff at line 18 of assignment_source.py: `queued: datetime = timezone.now()`. This is a dataclass field with a default value that is evaluated once at class definition time, not at instance creation time. This means all instances of AssignmentSource that don't explicitly provide a `queued` parameter will share the same timestamp from when the module was first loaded. This is a real bug that would cause incorrect queued-time metadata. The correct fix would be to use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead.
